en: Points of Controversy,
Great Fifty,
Sixth Chapter
The Discourse on the Formless Realms:
Is the base of infinite space unconditioned? Yes.
Is Nibbāna protection, a shelter, a refuge, a resort, the unshakable, and the deathless?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is the base of infinite space unconditioned, and is Nibbāna unconditioned?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are there two unconditioned things?
One should not say so …pe…
Are there two unconditioned things?
Yes. Are there two refuges? ... [and so on] ...
Does the intermediate space blow?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is the base of infinite space unconditioned?
“Yes.
“Is the base of infinite space existence, a destination, an abode of beings, saṃsāra, a matrix, a station of consciousness, and the acquisition of an individuality?
“Yes.”
Is the unconditioned (asaṅkhata) a state of existence (bhava), a destination (gati), an abode of beings (sattāvāsa), saṃsāra, a matrix (yoni), a station of consciousness (viññāṇaṭṭhiti),
or an acquisition of individuality (attabhāvapaṭilābha)? One should not say so… [as before]… Is there karma that leads to rebirth in the base of infinite space (ākāsānañcāyatana)?
“Yes.
“Then is there such a thing as karma that leads to the unconditioned?
“One should certainly not say so…” [and so on].
Is there a being who has reached the sphere of infinite space?
Yes. Is there a being who has reached the unconditioned? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it the case that beings are born,
grow old, die, pass away, and reappear in the sphere of infinite space? Yes.
Are beings born, age, die, pass away, and reappear in the unconditioned?
One should certainly not say so...
[and so on] ...Is there feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness in the base of infinite space?
“Yes,” [you say].
“In the unconditioned (asaṅkhata), there are feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness?
You should not speak thus …pe…
Is the base of infinite space a fourfold existence?
Yes. Is the unconditioned a fourfold existence? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said that “the four formless attainments are unconditioned”?
“Yes.
“But has it not been said by the Blessed One that the four formless attainments are ‘unwavering’?
“Yes.”
If the four formless attainments were spoken of by the Blessed One as being "unperturbed," then indeed, sir,
it must be said that "the four formless attainments are unconditioned.
The Discussion on the Formless is finished.
